title: Plant morphology
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What is the difference between a tendril and a leaf?
Can you show me an example of a modified stem?
How do different types of inflorescences look?

explain.say: Today we look at how plants change their parts.
Roots can change to help plants survive in different ways.
Stems sometimes change to help plants climb or store food.
Leaves can modify to become thorns or to help with movement.
Flowers are arranged in structures called inflorescences.
A real life example is how plants use these changes.

faq.q: Are all modifications of roots for storage?
faq.a: No, roots can modify for many things like support or even to trap insects. It depends on the plant's needs.
asks: What else can roots do besides store food?
Do roots always look different when they store food?

faq.q: How do I know if a stem modification is for support or storage?
faq.a: Think about its function in the plant. If it holds it up, it is for support. If you can eat it, it might be storage.
asks: Is there a test to check stem function?
What is the difference between a true stem and a modified one?

faq.a: Most thorns are modified stems, not leaves. However, some plants do have thorns from modified leaves, so it needs careful checking.
asks: What is the main difference between a thorn and a spine?
Can a leaf become a thorn?

faq.q: What is the difference between a raceme and an umbel?
faq.a: In a raceme, the flowers are attached to stalks along a main axis. In an umbel, the stalks all meet at a single point.
asks: Which inflorescence has flowers at the same level?
How do I tell the difference between these two groups?

faq.q: Do all plants have these types of modifications?
faq.a: No, only certain groups of plants show these specific types of modifications. Evolution drives these changes.
asks: Are these modifications universal in plants?
Why do plants need to change their parts?

facts: Roots can store food, forming structures like carrots.
Modified stems can function as support structures, like in vines.
Spines on cacti are modified leaves for defense.
Inflorescences are specialized arrangements of flowers.

quiz.say: A potato tuber is an example of which modification?
quiz.why: Potatoes are underground stems that store extra food for the plant.

wrong.0: Leaves are usually green and flat for photosynthesis, which the tuber is not.
wrong.1: An inflorescence is about flowers, not a storage organ.
wrong.3: While it is underground, the potato structure is a stem, not a root.

quiz.say: If a plant uses tendrils to grip a wall, what part is likely modified?
quiz.why: Tendrils are often modified leaves that help the plant climb to sunlight.

wrong.0: While stems can support, tendrils are more commonly derived from leaves.
wrong.1: Roots grow downwards into the soil, not for gripping structures like this.
wrong.2: Flower parts are related to reproduction, not climbing support.

quiz.say: Which arrangement has stalks meeting at a single point?
quiz.why: The umbel is characterized by all flower stalks radiating from one central point.

wrong.0: A raceme has flowers arranged sequentially along a main stalk.
wrong.1: This is too general; umbel is the specific pattern described.
wrong.2: A spire is a type of arrangement, but umbel describes the specific radial pattern.
